steps.title: Orbit (rotate your view)
steps.hint: Hold the middle mouse button and drag. Trackpad: swipe with two fingers, or drag the axis gizmo at the top-right of the viewport.

steps.title: Pan (slide your view)
steps.hint: Hold Shift + middle mouse button and drag. Trackpad: hold Shift and swipe with two fingers.

steps.title: Zoom in and out
steps.hint: Scroll the mouse wheel. Trackpad: pinch.

steps.title: Select an object
steps.hint: Left-click empty space to deselect, then left-click the cube.

steps.title: Move your mouse over the viewport and open the Add menu
steps.hint: Shortcut: Shift + A

steps.title: Choose Mesh, then Cube
steps.hint: Or use the button on the right. Shortcut: Shift + A > Mesh > Cube

steps.title: Click empty space to deselect, then click the cube to select it
steps.hint: A selected object has an orange outline. Shortcut: Left click

steps.title: Remove the selected object
steps.hint: (X also works, but asks you to confirm.) Shortcut: Delete

steps.title: Click empty space to deselect, then click an object to select it
steps.hint: If the scene is empty, add a cube first. Shortcut: Left click

steps.title: Press G to grab (move) the object
steps.hint: Move the mouse, then left-click to confirm, or press Esc to cancel. Shortcut: G

steps.title: To move along one direction only, press G, then X, Y or Z
steps.hint: Type a number such as 2 and press Enter for an exact distance. Shortcut: G, then X / Y / Z

steps.title: Press R to rotate
steps.hint: Move the mouse and click to confirm. Type a number to rotate by exact degrees. Shortcut: R

steps.title: Press S to scale
steps.hint: Move the mouse and click to confirm. Type a number such as 2 to double the size. Shortcut: S

steps.title: Made a mistake? Undo it
steps.hint: Shortcut: Ctrl + Z

steps.title: Click empty space to deselect, then click a mesh object such as a cube
steps.hint: Add one if the scene is empty. Shortcut: Left click

steps.title: Switch to Edit Mode
steps.hint: You will see dots (vertices), lines (edges) and faces that you can change. Shortcut: Tab

steps.title: Choose what to select: press 1 (vertices), 2 (edges), then 3 (faces)
steps.hint: The icons at the top of the viewport do the same. Shortcut: 1 / 2 / 3

steps.title: Press 3, click one face of the cube, then press G and move the mouse
steps.hint: Click to confirm. Shortcut: 3, click, G

steps.title: Return to Object Mode when you are done
steps.hint: Shortcut: Tab

steps.title: Select a cube and enter Edit Mode
steps.hint: Shortcut: Tab

steps.title: Press 3 for face selection, then click one face of the cube
steps.hint: Shortcut: 3, then click

steps.title: Press E to extrude
steps.hint: Move the mouse to pull the face outward, then left-click to confirm. Shortcut: E

steps.title: Leave Edit Mode to see the result
steps.hint: Shortcut: Tab

steps.title: Click empty space to deselect, then click the object you want to colour
steps.hint: Shortcut: Left click

steps.title: In the Properties editor on the right, open the Material tab (a round sphere icon near the bottom of the tab column)
steps.hint: Shortcut: Properties > Material tab

steps.title: Click New, then click the Base Color box and pick a colour
steps.hint: Shortcut: New > Base Color

steps.title: To see the colour in the viewport, switch to Material Preview (the third sphere icon at the top-right of the viewport)
steps.hint: Shortcut: Viewport shading buttons

steps.title: Select the default cube and delete it
steps.hint: Skip ahead automatically if the scene has no cube. Shortcut: Delete

steps.title: Add a new cube
steps.hint: Shortcut: Shift + A > Mesh > Cube

steps.title: With the cube selected, press S, then X, type 4 and press Enter
steps.hint: This stretches it into a wall about 8 metres long. Shortcut: S, X, 4, Enter

steps.title: Press S, then Y, type 0.2 and press Enter to make the wall thin
steps.hint: Shortcut: S, Y, 0.2, Enter

steps.title: Press S, then Z, type 1.5 and press Enter to make the wall taller
steps.hint: Shortcut: S, Z, 1.5, Enter

steps.title: Lift the wall so it sits on the ground: press G, then Z, type 1.5 and press Enter
steps.hint: The wall sinks below the ground grid after scaling. Shortcut: G, Z, 1.5, Enter

steps.title: Click empty space to deselect, then click the cube
steps.hint: Shortcut: Left click

steps.title: Press Shift + D, move the mouse and click to make a copy
steps.hint: The copy is a new object. Right-click or Esc keeps it in the same place. Shortcut: Shift + D

steps.title: Select both cubes: click one, then hold Shift and click the other
steps.hint: A selected object has an orange outline. Shortcut: Shift + Left click

steps.title: Click empty space to deselect, then press A to select everything
steps.hint: Shortcut: A

steps.title: Press Alt + A to deselect everything
steps.hint: On a Mac use Option + A. Shortcut: Alt + A

lessons.title: Look at your scene from every side

steps.title: Look from the front: press Numpad 1
steps.hint: No numpad? Use View > Viewpoint > Front, or the button on the right. Shortcut: Numpad 1

steps.title: Look from above: press Numpad 7
steps.hint: Shortcut: Numpad 7  (View > Viewpoint > Top)

steps.title: Switch between perspective and flat (orthographic) view: Numpad 5
steps.hint: Perspective looks like real life, orthographic keeps parallel lines parallel. Shortcut: Numpad 5

steps.title: Click the cube, then press Numpad . (period) to zoom to it
steps.hint: Great when you are lost in a big scene. Shortcut: Numpad . (View > Frame Selected)

steps.title: Add a sphere: Shift + A > Mesh > UV Sphere
steps.hint: Or use the button on the right. Shortcut: Shift + A > Mesh > UV Sphere

steps.title: Add a cylinder: Shift + A > Mesh > Cylinder
steps.hint: Shortcut: Shift + A > Mesh > Cylinder

steps.title: Add a flat plane: Shift + A > Mesh > Plane
steps.hint: A plane is a single flat square, good for floors. Shortcut: Shift + A > Mesh > Plane

steps.title: Add the Blender monkey: Shift + A > Mesh > Monkey
steps.hint: His name is Suzanne. Shortcut: Shift + A > Mesh > Monkey

lessons.title: See your model in different ways

steps.title: Show only the edges: press Shift + Z
steps.hint: Or click the first sphere icon at the top right of the viewport. Shortcut: Shift + Z

steps.title: Go back to solid view: press Shift + Z again
steps.hint: Or click the second sphere icon. Shortcut: Shift + Z

steps.title: See through objects: press Alt + Z
steps.hint: On a Mac use Option + Z. X-ray shows what is hidden inside. Shortcut: Alt + Z

steps.title: Show colours and light: choose Material Preview
steps.hint: The third sphere icon at the top right. Shortcut: Z, then Material Preview

steps.title: Click an object, then press F2 to rename it
steps.hint: Type a new name and press Enter. Good names save time later. Shortcut: F2

steps.title: Hide the selected object: press H
steps.hint: It is not deleted, only hidden. Shortcut: H

steps.title: Show everything again: press Alt + H
steps.hint: On a Mac use Option + H. Shortcut: Alt + H

steps.title: Put the object in a new collection: press M, then choose + New Collection
steps.hint: Collections are folders for objects. Type a name and click OK. Shortcut: M

steps.title: Add a sphere: Shift + A > Mesh > UV Sphere
steps.hint: Or use the button on the right. Shortcut: Shift + A > Mesh > UV Sphere

steps.title: Make it look smooth: right-click it and choose Shade Smooth
steps.hint: Or Object > Shade Smooth. This only changes how light falls on it.

steps.title: Add more detail: press Ctrl + 2
steps.hint: This adds a Subdivision Surface modifier, level 2. Shortcut: Ctrl + 2

steps.title: Add even more detail: press Ctrl + 3
steps.hint: Higher numbers are smoother but heavier for your computer. Shortcut: Ctrl + 3

lessons.title: Edit Mode tools: loop cut, inset, bevel

steps.title: Select a cube and enter Edit Mode
steps.hint: Add a cube if the scene is empty. Shortcut: Tab

steps.title: Add a loop cut: press Ctrl + R, hover over the cube, click, then right-click
steps.hint: Scroll the mouse wheel before clicking for more cuts. Shortcut: Ctrl + R

steps.title: Inset a face: press 3, click a face, press I, move the mouse and click
steps.hint: This draws a smaller face inside the face. Shortcut: I

steps.title: Round the edges: press 2, press A, press Ctrl + B, move the mouse and click
steps.hint: Scroll the mouse wheel to make the edges rounder. Shortcut: Ctrl + B

steps.title: Return to Object Mode
steps.hint: Shortcut: Tab

steps.title: Click empty space to deselect, then click the object
steps.hint: Shortcut: Left click

steps.title: Open the Material tab in the Properties editor
steps.hint: The round sphere icon near the bottom of the tab column. Click New if it has no material.

steps.title: Make it metal: set Metallic to 1
steps.hint: Drag the Metallic slider to the right, or double-click it and type 1.

steps.title: Make it shiny: set Roughness to 0.1
steps.hint: Low roughness is a mirror, high roughness is matt. Drag the slider left or type 0.1.

steps.title: To see it, switch to Material Preview
steps.hint: The third sphere icon at the top right of the viewport.

steps.title: Have two cubes in the scene
steps.hint: Click 'Add a cube', or Shift + A > Mesh > Cube. They appear in the same place.

steps.title: Click empty space, then press A to select everything
steps.hint: Shortcut: A

steps.title: Join them into one object: press Ctrl + J
steps.hint: Shortcut: Ctrl + J (Object > Join)

steps.title: Split them again: Tab, A, P, choose By Loose Parts, then Tab
steps.hint: Edit Mode is needed for splitting. Shortcut: P

steps.title: Add text: Shift + A > Text
steps.hint: Shortcut: Shift + A > Text

steps.title: Change the words: press Tab, Backspace, type, then Tab
steps.hint: You are typing inside the object. Press Tab when you are done.

steps.title: Make it 3D: Data tab > Geometry > Extrude, type 0.2
steps.hint: The green letter 'a' tab in the Properties editor.

steps.title: Add a light: Shift + A > Light > Sun
steps.hint: Without light a picture is dark. Shortcut: Shift + A > Light > Sun

steps.title: Look through the camera: press Numpad 0
steps.hint: No numpad? View > Cameras > Active Camera. The camera is what the picture sees.

steps.title: Take the picture: press F12
steps.hint: A new window shows your image. Close it when you are done. Shortcut: F12

steps.title: Click empty space to deselect, then click the cube
steps.hint: Shortcut: Left click

steps.title: Save its position as a keyframe: press I
steps.hint: The Timeline at the bottom shows a yellow diamond. Shortcut: I

steps.title: Jump to frame 60: click or drag in the Timeline numbers
steps.hint: Frame 60 is about 2 seconds later.

steps.title: Move the cube (G), then press I again
steps.hint: Blender fills in everything between the two keyframes.

steps.title: Play it: hover over the viewport and press Space
steps.hint: Press Space again to stop.

lessons.title: Final project: build a tiny house

steps.title: Delete the default cube
steps.hint: Click it, then press Delete. We start from an empty floor.

steps.title: Add a plane for the ground and make it big
steps.hint: Shift + A > Mesh > Plane, then press S, type 4, press Enter.

steps.title: Add a cube for the house and lift it onto the ground
steps.hint: Shift + A > Mesh > Cube, then G, Z, 1, Enter. (The cube is 2 m tall.)

steps.title: Add a cone for the roof and put it on top
steps.hint: Shift + A > Mesh > Cone, then G, Z, 3, Enter.

steps.title: Colour at least two objects
steps.hint: Select an object, Material tab > New > Base Color. Try red for the roof.

steps.title: Take a picture of your house: press F12
steps.hint: Your first finished scene. Well done!
